headline: 260 days at sea. Eight sailors attempted suicide.
summary: Eight sailors with the USS Abraham Lincoln attempted suicide on a deployment that kept the carrier at sea a record 260-plus days for the Iran war, acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand. None died. The ship carried a psychologist and a therapy dog, Cao says. Gillibrand calls the conditions "serious and deteriorating."

cover_question.q: Why were they at sea so long?

cover_answer: The Iran war. Their trip home kept getting pushed back.
table_question: How long is too long to be away from home for work?

5-7.script: Some sailors on a giant ship have been away from home since last November, about as long as a whole school year, and a few of them got so sad they tried to hurt themselves. Nobody died. The ship has doctors on it and even a therapy dog, and it is sailing home now. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. A five-year-old takes one vivid piece for the whole story, so give them the ship coming home, with a dog on it.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old reads your face before the words and keeps one vivid piece of the whole event, so the script gives them the ship, a school year away, a dog on board, and the trip home. Cantor found this age fears what could reach them, so nothing here lands at your house. Expect "why were they sad?" Being away that long is hard.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: The Lincoln left San Diego in November, due home in May. The Iran war kept pushing that back, until it hit a record 260 days at sea. A deployment is a countdown, and every time the end moved, the crew started over. Eight sailors got so low they tried to end their lives. None died.
8-12.why: Leave, get extended, start the countdown again: a chain in order.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out cause and effect, so the script runs the chain: a ship leaves, the war moves the return date, the crew starts the countdown again. The countdown is a mechanism they run themselves, and it shows how a delay becomes a weight. Expect "why didn't they just come home?" Sailors go where they are ordered.

13-17.script: Eight suicide attempts among 6,000 sailors over 10 months: a scandal, or, as one psychiatrist says, actually low? Second: Trump called nine months at sea "a good period of time." Gillibrand calls the conditions "serious and deteriorating." What would settle it?
13-17.why: One number, two readings. Let them weigh it before you do.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: eight in 6,000 is a low rate, and eight sailors tried to die. The script hands them both, plus a psychiatrist who says the count is not the point, then two adults describing one ship, so they practise weighing sources. Expect "who's right?" Cao's letter says both: care on board, and things that broke.

5-7.a: Most are. The ones who got very sad got help from doctors on the ship, and everyone is sailing home now.

8-12.q: Why were they at sea so long?
8-12.a: The Iran war. Due home in May, the ship was kept out until it hit 260 days.

8-12.q: Did they run out of food?
8-12.a: No. Fighting made resupply hard, so for a short time one meal choice instead of two.

13-17.a: Out of 6,000 it's low, a psychiatrist says. But something upset those families.

13-17.q: Why did the president say it was fine?
13-17.a: He called nine months at sea 'a good period of time.' Gillibrand calls that disrespect.
